At new and full moon the lunar and solar tidal forces act in the same direction and add up, producing a spring tide with the largest range; at the quarter moons they are perpendicular, giving a neap tide with the smallest range. A semidiurnal tide rises and falls about twice a day, with a period near 12 hours 25 minutes.
